status.stage: Completed: learned selection reduces drift; deformation remains inaccurate
status.detail: OSMO experiment particle-gnn-region-1 completed on four L40 GPUs. The final comparison uses 12 previously unused test trajectories: four rest, four sustained pushes, and four continuous drags. All 48 test rollouts completed without invalid states or graph overflow.
findings: Conclusion: region selection substantially reduces artificial motion of stationary sand. Median five-second particle position RMSE fell from 7.09 cm to 1.63 cm. Across the 12 trajectories, 72,740 of 72,764 reference-stationary particles moved more than 1 cm with the original GNN; learned selection reduced that count to 162 (0.22%).

The improvement is not sufficient to establish accurate deformation. The learned selector beats frozen particles on 5 of 12 trajectories. Its median error on particles displaced more than 1 cm is 3.47 cm, compared with 2.39 cm for frozen particles. A simple velocity threshold gives 1.83 cm overall RMSE, only modestly worse than the learned selector at 1.63 cm.

Reference-motion selection gives 0.74 cm median overall RMSE and 1.95 cm error on displaced particles; it beats frozen particles on 11 of 12 trajectories. This comparison uses future MPM positions and is not deployable. It demonstrates useful improvement from better activity decisions, even with the motion GNN weights fixed.

Training: 776 trajectories; classification calibration: 109 validation trajectories. Two classifiers were trained for 6,000 updates each. Six recurrent validation rollouts selected the 0.5 mm displacement label over 0.1 s. The selected checkpoint is update 5,000, with activity probability threshold 0.6. No test trajectories were used for training, checkpoint selection or threshold calibration.

Implementation: a 48-input, two-hidden-layer classifier (64 units per hidden layer, SiLU activation; 7,361 parameters) predicts activity. Inputs include three particle velocity states, material features, local rigid-surface geometry and relative velocity, neighborhood size, and neighboring particle speeds. Small velocities are scaled before classification. The position update and inactive-particle freezing run on the GPU; the original GNN still processes the complete graph.

Why does the learned selector remain worse than reference-motion selection? A post-test diagnostic used the same 750 frames from test trajectories #117, #453 and #460, with the selected weights and threshold unchanged. With reference particle states, activity precision was 80.5% and recall 93.5%. With recurrent GNN particle states, precision fell to 28.8% and recall to 53.6%. Accumulated particle-state errors therefore degrade the activity decisions. Good classification on reference states alone is insufficient.

The next development step is training with recurrent predicted particle states and evaluating deformation accuracy as well as stationary-particle drift. Restricting graph computation to active particles should follow accuracy validation; this experiment does not demonstrate a computational speedup.

The three test videos were selected before inspecting their errors: #117 continuous drag, #453 sustained push, and #460 rest. Both views replay the same recorded box motion. Only the particle trajectory differs. Local playback with the full-dataset selector completed all 250 steps on the RTX 5090.

visuals.caption: Independent test comparison. The dashed line in the middle panel is the frozen-particle error. The reference-selection method uses future MPM data; the other methods use available state information.

Test trajectory #117: continuous dragging. Left: MPM reference. Right: GNN with learned activity selection. Both replay the same recorded box motion. Five-second particle position RMSE: 5.63 cm. Stationary particles drifting over 1 cm: 24 of 4935.

Test trajectory #453: sustained pushing. Left: MPM reference. Right: GNN with learned activity selection. Both replay the same recorded box motion. Five-second particle position RMSE: 1.56 cm. Stationary particles drifting over 1 cm: 12 of 6141.

Test trajectory #460: rest. Left: MPM reference. Right: GNN with learned activity selection. Both replay the same recorded box motion. Five-second particle position RMSE: 1.51 cm. Stationary particles drifting over 1 cm: 15 of 6271.
